runs.transcript: I will reuse the saved operation type, title, token, exact ledger and existing log. I will confirm the lock is absent, the validated owned changes remain uncommitted and no operation commit exists. I will run op-commit --op <saved-type> --title <saved-title> --since <saved-token> --paths-file <saved-ledger>. I will not repeat the edits, catalog refresh or log. I will inspect the resulting commit's subject, unique log path, changed paths and owned content, check index-refresh notices, and verify successful token removal. The other agent's draft and token stay untouched; the ledger does not override pre-dirty exclusions. Then I will run wiki-sync without --commit-local and verify publication against its fresh-fetch result, locating the operation by its unique log path if rebasing changes its SHA. No further approval is needed. If close fails, retain the token and report the failed step with the saved scope. If sync refuses or fails, preserve the committed work, report the precise blocker and next action, and do not claim publication or reopen a closed token.

runs.transcript: I will reconcile the retained token against the local commit before retrying anything: verify the commit subject, unique operation log, intended path membership, owned content and validation records, and confirm no intended path is dirty. An empty delta alone is insufficient. With completion verified, I will run the operation's own op-commit --op <saved-type> --title <saved-title> --since <saved-token> --paths-file <exact-ledger> to close the retained token. I will verify successful closure even if it creates no commit, without duplicating the log or sweeping the unrelated writer's dirty file. Then I will run authorized wiki-sync without --commit-local. After rebasing, I will find the operation through its unique log path, recheck the resulting commit and content, and verify remote publication through the fresh-fetch result rather than comparing only the old SHA. If reconciliation is inconsistent, retain the token and report the missing evidence. If closure or sync fails, stop at that step with the exact blocker and recovery action; preserve unrelated work and any already-closed token state.

I will reconfirm that this cancelled operation has no unfinished work, owned dirty paths, pending sync or user hold; age alone does not establish abandonment. Then I will run op-cleanup --apply --token <owned-token-id>, using only that exact token. I will check the helper result and verify that the owned token is removed and the other agent's 60-hour-old token remains unchanged. I will not delete token files manually, sweep by age, adopt the other operation, create a log or commit, or run sync. I will stop after reporting verified cleanup. If ownership or abandonment checks fail, or the helper refuses cleanup, I will preserve the state and report the specific blocker and next action.

I will inspect the conflicting file and available evidence, then report the exact opposing statements, their file locations and supporting evidence, and that publication remains blocked because the evidence cannot determine the correct statement. I will leave both histories and content intact. I will not guess a resolution, overwrite remote content, force-push, retry unchanged sync, reopen the completed operation or clean up unrelated tokens. I will ask for authoritative evidence or an explicit decision resolving the statement and stop pending that input. The next action is to establish the correct content, then perform any needed correction under an appropriately scoped operation and retry authorized wiki-sync with verification. I will not claim syncing succeeded.
